To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spin-polarized electric currents are generated in semimagnetic and nonmagnetic semiconductor heterostructures under the influence of an external magnetic field and mw radiation.
spin polarized electric currents are generated in semimagnetic and nonmagnetic quantum wells by mw radiation in the presence of an in-plane magnetic field.
mw-induced electric currents in semiconductor structures are spin-polarized and can be tuned by the external magnetic field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the generation and transport of spin polarized electric currents induced by the application of mw radiation to semiconductor heterostructures.
the spin polarized electric currents (SPEIC) induced in semiconductor heterostructure by mw radiation and the possibility of their use for the spintronic device applications.
the generation and detection of spin-polarized currents in semiconductor heterostuctures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin polarization of the electrons in the quantum well is the key to understanding the current generation by mw radiation in the presence of an external magnetic field.
the spin-dependent energy-relaxation mechanism is the dominant mechanism for the observed microwave-induced electric current in semimagnetic and nonmagnetic quantum well structures.
the microwave radiation induced electric currents are a consequence of the spin-dependent electron energy relaxation in semiconductors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mw radiation induced spin polarization of the electron gas in a magnetic field leads to a spin-polarized current in the direction of the applied field.
we were able to generate spin-polarized currents in semimagnetics, which is an important first step toward spintronics.
we have demonstrated the generation of electric current in semiconductor quantum wells by mw radiation, which opens the possibility of using mw radiation as an energy source for spintronics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spin polarization of the electric current can be controlled by the mw power and frequency.
the spin polarization of the electric current is determined by the relative magnitudes of the Zeeman splitting and the electron temperature.
the spin-dependent energy loss is not only important in the generation of spin currents but also in the generation of charge currents.
